findings.title: LLM Prompt Injection Risk
findings.description: User-controlled or retrieved content may override, bypass, or manipulate model instructions.
findings.business_impact: Prompt injection can bypass controls, disclose hidden context, or manipulate tool actions and responses.
remediation: Treat user-supplied and retrieved content as untrusted data and keep it structurally separate from system/developer instructions.
Do not let model-generated text directly authorize privileged tool calls; enforce server-side authorization and least privilege for every tool action.
Validate model outputs before executing commands, sending requests, changing records, or exposing sensitive context.
Add adversarial regression tests for instruction override, indirect prompt injection, data exfiltration, and unauthorized tool use.
findings.recommended_action: Separate system, developer, retrieved, and user content using role-aware message boundaries. Treat retrieved documents and user prompts as untrusted input and never let them override system instructions.

rule_contract.title: LLM Prompt Injection Risk

remediation: Separate system, developer, retrieved, and user content using role-aware message boundaries.

Log and monitor prompt-injection attempts and test known jailbreak patterns during release validation.

Add masking/encryption at sinks and enforce data minimisation in API responses.
Map each sensitive flow to owner, purpose, retention, and approved processing basis.
